stories.headline: Andhra Pradesh: 280 employees skip election duty in Krishna, get show cause notices
stories.title: Andhra Pradesh: 280 employees skip election duty in Krishna, get show cause notices
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Krishna district election authority in Andhra Pradesh has issued show-cause notices to 280 employees who failed to report for election duty during the local body polls on November 26.
They have been asked to submit explanations with supporting evidence by 6 pm on November 27.

District Election Officer and Collector DK Balaji said on Thursday, November 26, that 74 employees assigned to municipal election duties and 206 assigned to gram panchayat polls were absent without prior permission.
Among the 74 municipal employees, 16 were presiding officers, 12 assistant presiding officers, and 46 other polling officers.
Gudivada municipality accounted for 45 absentees, including 11 presiding officers, five assistant presiding officers, and 29 other polling officers.
In Tadigadapa municipality, 29 employees were absent, comprising five presiding officers, seven assistant presiding officers, and 17 other polling officers.
The 206 employees who failed to report for the first phase of gram panchayat elections included 119 presiding officers and 87 other polling officers.
Gannavaram had the highest number of absentees at 62, followed by Unguturu with 42, Gudivada with 39, Bapulapadu with 29, Gudlavalleru with 24, and Nandivada with 10.
Balaji said the employees were required to report at their designated distribution centres on November 25 to collect election material before proceeding to their allotted polling stations.
Those who fail to provide satisfactory explanations and supporting evidence will face disciplinary action.
The notices come as the first phase of gram panchayat elections in six mandals of Krishna district recorded a voter turnout of 79.77% on November 26.
Of the 2,63,603 registered voters, 2,10,270 cast their votes.

stories.headline: India-US trade deal close to completion: Goyal amid fresh tariff threat
stories.title: India-US trade deal close to completion: Goyal amid fresh tariff threat
stories.summary: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal on Friday said the India-US trade deal is nearing completion, with the process and roadmap for finalising the pact, which had earlier held up negotiations, now taking shape. "The US trade deal is close to culmination. The process and pathway, which was always something which held back finalising the deal, is now taking some shape," Goyal said while addressing the India Debt Capital Market Summit 2026 virtually. The remarks came after the latest US Trade Representative's (USTR) report proposed 25 per cent tariffs on imports from India, with a provision to cap them at 17 per cent if the two countries agree to a bilateral trade deal, giving it a slight edge over Asian competitors.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Appreciates Sucheta Dalal's PIL On Unclaimed Financial Assets, Disposes Plea Noting Measures Taken By Authorities
stories.title: Supreme Court Appreciates Sucheta Dalal's PIL On Unclaimed Financial Assets, Disposes Plea Noting Measures Taken By Authorities
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday disposed of a Public Interest Litigation filed by financial journalist Sucheta Dalal seeking directions to authorities to put in place measures enabling legal heirs to trace and claim unclaimed financial assets, including bank deposits, shares and mutual fund investments.

Noting that the Union Government, the Reserve Bank of India and the Securities and Exchange Board of India have taken various administrative and regulatory steps to address the issue, the bench of Justice Vikram Nath and Justice R Mahadevan observed that judicial directions in that regard are not necessary.
At the same time, the bench placed on record its appreciation for Dalal for taking up a genuine public cause, saying that the case was an example of a responsible use of public interest litigation.
The bench also appreciated Advocate Prashant Bhushan for espousing the petitioners' cause with "passion and perseverance."

"The present proceedings were instituted not for securing any personal benefit but with the objective of protecting the financial interests of countless depositors, investors and their lawful claimants.
The petitioner has consistently drawn attention to the difficulties faced by ordinary citizens in identifying and recovering the unclaimed financial assets.
The concerns raised were genuine and the pursuit of the appropriate institutional measures to address them reflects a responsible exercise of public interest litigation," the bench observed.
However, the Court noted that the principal concerns raised have been substantially addressed by measures undertaken by the respondents (SEBI, RBI and the Department of Economic Affairs).

"We take on record the statements and assurances made in the respondents affidavits and expect the concerned authorities to continue the efforts towards improving the accessibility, efficiency, and transparency of the mechanism for identifying and recovering unclaimed financial assets.
No useful purpose will be served by keeping the petition pending for further monitoring of the regulatory measures already undertaken.
Any specific grievances concerning unclaimed financial assets may be pursued before the competent authority in accordance with law," the bench added.
The bench had reserved judgment on November 17.

stories.headline: CUKashmir celebrates Constitution Day-2026
stories.title: CUKashmir celebrates Constitution Day-2026
stories.summary: Ganderbal, Nov 26: Department of Law, School of Legal Studies (SLS), Central University of Kashmir (CUKashmir), celebrated the Constitution Day-2026 under the theme “Hamara Samvidhan-Hamara Swabhiman” at Tulmulla campus here on Thursday. The programme commemorated the adoption of the Constitution of India and reaffirmed the University's commitment to constitutional values and the principles enshrined in the founding document. In his keynote address (Online), former Judge, Punjab and Haryana High Court, Justice Paramjit Singh Dhaliwal deliberated extensively on the concept of constitutionalism and the evolution of the basic structure doctrine, describing them as essential safeguards for preserving the constitutional framework. Drawing upon his extensive experience in the legal profession, he shared insights into the relationship between the Constitution, the legislature, the executive and the judiciary. He observed that constitutionalism was reflected not merely in judicial pronouncements but also in the conduct of citizens and public institutions, particularly in their commitment to uphold the rule of law. He elaborated upon the historical evolution of the relationship between Parliament and the judiciary concerning the power to amend the Constitution, tracing important judicial developments from the early constitutional cases to the landmark Kesavananda Bharati judgment of 1973. Justice Dhaliwal also reflected upon the warnings articulated by Dr. B. R. Ambedkar in his concluding address to the Constituent Assembly, particularly against unconstitutional methods in politics and the absence of social democracy. He urged law students to develop independent thinking, engage critically with constitutional questions and support their arguments with reason and sound legal understanding. He emphasised that the true strength of constitutional democracy depended not only upon the institutions established under the Constitution, but also upon the integrity, awareness and conduct of those who served and upheld it. Earlier, in his welcome address, Dean School of Legal Studies, Prof. Farooq Ahmad Mir emphasised that Constitution Day was not merely a ceremonial occasion but an opportunity to reflect upon the responsibilities that the Constitution places upon every citizen. Highlighting the significance of engaging students in the process of social transformation, he observed that meaningful change in society could be achieved only when students, teachers and families collectively became instruments of positive change. Referring to the Preamble, he underscored that the Constitution belongs to every citizen, irrespective of caste, creed, religion, region or language. He highlighted its commitment to securing social, economic and political justice, liberty of thought and expression, equality of status and opportunity, and fraternity, assuring the dignity of the individual and the unity and integrity of the nation. Tracing the making of the Constitution, Prof. Mir observed that it was the outcome of immense intellectual effort, deliberations and the sacrifices associated with India's freedom struggle. He noted that the Constituent Assembly took two years, eleven months and eighteen days to complete the historic task, with its members engaging in extensive discussions and deliberations before giving the country its Constitution. He further observed that the Constitution was a dynamic document whose relevance continued to be strengthened through judicial interpretation in response to the changing needs of society. The programme proceedings were conducted by Assistant Prof. Dr. Gulafroz Jan, who also read the Preamble to the Constitution, with the participants reaffirming their commitment to its ideals. Associate Professor Dr. Jehirul Islam proposed the vote of thanks. The Constitution Day Preamble reading and pledge-taking exercise were also organised across all campuses of the University. Meanwhile, the Directorate of Students Welfare also organised a debate competition as part of the Constitution Day Celebrations.

stories.headline: Centre sanctions Rs 50L for model Sub-Registrar office
stories.title: Centre sanctions Rs 50L for model Sub-Registrar office
stories.summary: Vijayawada MP Kesineni Sivanath announces Rs 50 lakh first-phase sanction for a PSK-model Sub-Registrar office under DILRMP 3.0 and NAKSHA schemes.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Vijayawada MP Kesineni Sivanath announces Rs 50 lakh first-phase sanction for a PSK-model Sub-Registrar office under DILRMP 3.0 and NAKSHA schemes.

The Centre has sanctioned Rs.50 lakh in the first phase for setting up a state-of-the-art model Sub-Registrar office in Vijayawada on the lines of a Passport Seva Kendra (PSK), Vijayawada MP Kesineni Sivanath (Chinni) announced on Thursday.
Welcoming the decision, the MP said the Centre had responded positively to his repeated representations to Union Ministers seeking improved property registration facilities for people in Vijayawada.

The proposed model office will be established under the Digital India Land Records Modernisation Programme (DILRMP) 3.0 and NAKSHA schemes, aimed at modernising land records and improving registration-related services.
